data.title: Implement LATER.3 — opt-in self-hoster telemetry (heartbeat phone-home)
data.description:
Founder greenlit 2026-06-13 (chose 'build now' over park/defer/kill in /sal triage), ahead of the LATER.3 gate. Placed in NEXT (not NOW) so it does NOT displace the demo (local-61) + live in-browser pass (local-62), which remain the critical path — bump to NOW on request.

### What this is (and is NOT)
A FULLY OPT-IN phone-home so the PROJECT can count self-hosted installs. This is a DIFFERENT channel from the shipped PostHog analytics:
- Shipped PostHog (posthog/client.ts + server.ts) = the OPERATOR's own engagement data, sent to whoever sets VITE_POSTHOG_KEY / POSTHOG_API_KEY. A fresh install with no key sends the project NOTHING — so it yields zero count of independent self-hosters.
- This item = a heartbeat to a PROJECT-owned sink so independent self-hosters are countable. Default OFF; never fires without explicit opt-in.

### Resolved architecture (Option A — low-infra, reuses posthog-node)
- Sink: a PROJECT-owned PostHog INGEST key (phc_..., the public write-only kind ALREADY shipped to browsers via VITE_POSTHOG_KEY — baking it into the image is consistent with PostHog's model, NOT a secret leak). New env SYNEK_TELEMETRY_KEY (project default can be baked at build), distinct from the operator's POSTHOG_API_KEY.
- Opt-in: new env SYNEK_TELEMETRY (default OFF). Heartbeat fires ONLY when truthy. Env flag, not a first-run dark pattern — the honest shape for a CLI/Docker product.
- Event: one `self_host_heartbeat`, distinctId = a persisted random install id (a settings/meta row in the DB, generated once on the data volume). Properties { version, db_backend (sqlite|pg), first_seen_at }. NO graph content, NO user PII, NO timeline ids.
- Cadence: fire once per server boot (counts active installs over time). Optional daily re-ping later.
- Wire: emit from the server boot path (src/lib/db/index.ts boot or scripts/serve-build.ts) reusing posthog/server.ts captureServer + the existing flush/shutdown plumbing.

### One decision for Kael to ratify (step 1, NON-blocking)
Confirm Option A (project PostHog ingest key) vs Option B (a dedicated minimal ingest endpoint the project owns). Recommended: A. Residual risk of A = a bad actor extracting the public key and inflating the count with fake heartbeats — acceptable for a vanity self-hoster metric; mitigate with a tight property schema. B removes that risk but is new infra to run. Pick A unless count integrity is load-bearing.

### Privacy / positioning
The 'no telemetry' landing copy was already removed when PostHog landed. Add a short, EXACT privacy note (README + landing): what the heartbeat contains, that it is opt-in/default-off, and the one env flag to enable it.

### Acceptance criteria
- Default install (no SYNEK_TELEMETRY) sends ZERO bytes to the project sink — verified.
- With SYNEK_TELEMETRY=1, exactly one self_host_heartbeat fires per boot with { install_id, version, db_backend } and no PII/graph data.
- install_id persists across container/volume recreate (lives on the data volume) and is stable per install.
- A verify script (verify:telemetry) asserts opt-out (no key/flag = no client) and the payload shape, mirroring verify:mcp's data-layer style.
- Privacy note documents the exact payload.

### Refs
docs/product/roadmap.md (LATER.3 / 2.6); reuses src/lib/posthog/server.ts; ships naturally inside the self-host image (local-99) but works on any install. Was the LATER.3 placeholder; fleshed into a build spec in place 2026-06-13.

### Done 2026-06-13 (build-verified; live pass owed via local-62)
Shipped: src/lib/telemetry/heartbeat.ts — opt-in gate (SYNEK_TELEMETRY truthy AND SYNEK_TELEMETRY_KEY present, else silent), anonymous payload { install_id = domain-separated sha256(BETTER_AUTH_SECRET), version, db_backend }, one self_host_heartbeat via posthog-node (flushAt:1 + shutdown), fire-and-forget, never throws. Wired at the prod boot seam scripts/serve-build.ts (.listen -> void sendHeartbeat()) so it fires once per server boot, NOT on dev/seed/stdio. Dockerfile bakes the project ingest key via ARG/ENV SYNEK_TELEMETRY_KEY (public write-only phc_ key; the opt-in FLAG is NOT baked, so a default image is silent until the operator runs with -e SYNEK_TELEMETRY=1). .env.example documented; README 'no telemetry' claim corrected to the honest 'nothing leaves your machine unless you turn it on' + a telemetry bullet. DEVIATION from the spec's 'persisted random install id on the data volume': used a DERIVED sha256(secret) id instead — zero migration, no second DB connection at the boot seam, identical for sqlite/pg; caveat = rotating BETTER_AUTH_SECRET reads as a new install (acceptable for a vanity count, undercount-only). Verified: verify:telemetry (13 asserts) + typecheck + build green; boot smoke test serves HTTP 200 with telemetry OFF. Deferred within item: the lovable-gate self-report upgrade (gate local-63 stays self-report).

data.title: Implement GLOBE G1 — data contract: lat/lng on NodeMetadata + apply_patch + layout report
data.description:

- Add `lat?: number`/`lng?: number` to `NodeMetadata` (schema.ts) + `GraphNode` DTO (domain/types.ts). JSON metadata column → NO migration.

- MCP ops (mcp/ops.ts): add `lat` (z.number().min(-90).max(90).optional()) + `lng` (min(-180).max(180)) to add_node AND update_node opSchema branches with describe() hints; merge into metadata assembly (additive, pair-guarded).
- warnings.ts: lone-coordinate (lat without lng or vice versa) + null-island (0,0) per-patch warnings via coordinateWarnings(ops) wired into collectPatchWarnings. NO ocean/landmass check (deferred — needs server TopoJSON).
- layout-report.ts: new `coordinates` section { total, located, coveragePct, hasLocationNoCoords, sample[12] } after nodeIndex build.
- node-verb-prompts.ts: buildGlobeBackfillPrompt (so the backfill loop works before the globe renders).

### Done when
apply_patch accepts+validates lat/lng; get_layout_report returns coordinates section; Patch undo restores coords for free (metadata snapshot); typecheck + build green; no migration.

data.title: Self-host Docker image — single-user, SQLite-on-a-volume
data.description:
A portable container that runs the existing local-first Core on any box (VPS or cloud) with NO Postgres swap — distinct from local-18 (NEXT.4 Postgres + Compose), which stays the later scale-up. Founder chose the SQLite-on-volume path 2026-06-12 ('just give me the Dockerfile').

### Built this session (working tree, build-verified)
- `Dockerfile` — multi-stage `node:22-bookworm-slim` (NOT Bun: better-sqlite3 needs the Node ABI). Build stage: python3/make/g++ + `npm install` + `npm run build`. Runtime stage: no compilers, carries dist/ + drizzle/ + node_modules (incl. the compiled .node + tsx). `CMD npm start`, HEALTHCHECK on `/`, `VOLUME /data`.
- `.dockerignore` — excludes node_modules/dist/*.db/.env so host data + secrets never bake into the image.
- `package.json` `start` script (`tsx scripts/serve-build.ts`) — promotes the e2e prod server to the real entry; `docker:build`.
- Migration-on-boot fix (src/lib/db/index.ts): the old `migrate(...)` used a source-relative `../../../drizzle` that does NOT resolve in the bundled `dist/server/server.js`, wrapped in a SILENT catch — i.e. a fresh prod DB could boot un-migrated and serve an empty schema. Now keys on `SYNEK_MIGRATIONS_DIR` (set to /app/drizzle in the image) → repo-relative → <cwd>/drizzle, validated against `meta/_journal.json`, and FAILS LOUD in production instead of swallowing.

### Done when
`docker build` green (verifying this session); `docker run -v synek-data:/data -e BETTER_AUTH_SECRET -e BETTER_AUTH_URL` boots, applies migrations to the mounted volume, serves the canvas + `/api/mcp` on the mapped port, and data survives a container recreate. Single writer only — one container, no concurrent stdio server, no horizontal scale.

### Constraint
Manual node-image uploads are stored INLINE as base64 data URLs in node JSON (src/lib/files.ts), so no object storage is needed — but the SQLite file grows with media; factor into the volume size + backups (local-103).

### Done 2026-06-13
Closed by the founder; verified on main. Image + migrate-on-boot fix committed in a6bf42a: Dockerfile (multi-stage node:22, tsx via scripts/serve-build.ts, VOLUME /data, healthcheck), .dockerignore, and the SYNEK_MIGRATIONS_DIR fail-loud migration fix in src/lib/db/index.ts are all present. DOCKER VERIFIED (note local-104): builds, boots ~5s, 18 migrations applied to the mounted volume, /api/mcp -> 401, data survives a container recreate. Image done; the remaining self-host work is the deploy chain local-100/101/102/103 -> Rook.

data.title: Implement GLOBE-S GS2 — zoom the globe (wheel + pinch + controls + ⌘K) with a shared rAF ease
data.description:
Globe Story Mode primitive #1. The globe has NO zoom today — projection scale is fixed at `(Math.min(viewW, size.h)/2) * 0.92` (GlobeLens.tsx:255). Add a clamped zoom and a reusable camera ease that GS1 (story-driven globe) leans on. Refs: docs/product/prd/globe-stories.md §GS2.

### Scope
- Add `zoom` state (multiplier, default 1) to GlobeLens; projection scale becomes `… * 0.92 * zoom`. Clamp `zoom ∈ [1, ~6]` (1 = whole sphere fits; upper bound a UX call).
- Wheel: `onWheel` on the globe SVG, preventDefault, `zoom *= exp(-deltaY*k)`, clamp. Trackpad pinch arrives as wheel+ctrlKey — same handler, larger k. (No touch/two-finger — desktop-targeted per the guardrail.)
- Controls: a +/− zoom control group (bottom-left, mirroring React Flow's Controls) + ⌘K NAV actions 'Globe: zoom in / out / reset'.
- Factor the rotation-ease lerp currently living INSIDE the play rAF loop (GlobeLens.tsx:170–177) into an always-available rAF ease that runs whenever there's a pending rotation OR zoom target — so button/⌘K zooms glide AND a beat step (GS1) can animate the camera with playback paused. Raw wheel can apply immediately (no ease).
- A manual zoom (like a manual drag, GlobeLens.tsx:232) sets `userRotatedRef` (the 'user took over' flag) so an in-progress story-follow doesn't yank the camera mid-gesture.
- Optional: `globe_zoomed { timeline_id, via }` analytics via the existing capture seam (low priority).

### Done when
Wheel + trackpad-pinch zoom the globe within clamp; +/− control and ⌘K zoom in/out/reset work; zoom + drag both glide via the shared ease and both suspend story-follow; typecheck + build green; verify:globe + globe e2e unregressed; drag-rotate + click→panel unchanged.

### Done 2026-06-13
Shipped (build + e2e verified; uncommitted). Clamped zoom [1,6] on GlobeLens: a non-passive wheel listener (passive:false — React onWheel is passive; trackpad pinch via ctrlKey, coarser k), a left-center +/−/reset control group, and ⌘K 'Globe: zoom in/out/reset' via an imperative controlsRef handle the lazy lens registers into (TimelineCanvas.globeControlsRef → CommandPalette.globeZoom, gated on lensView==='globe'). The GS1 per-beat ease was generalized into ONE shared camera ease (easeCameraTo → nonce-driven rAF) that all programmatic moves funnel through; raw wheel/drag bypass it (immediate + cancelEase). Manual zoom flags userRotatedRef (re-arms next beat via the cursor-skip effect). Reduced-motion snaps. OQ-S2 resolved: zoom-to-center for v1. New globe_zoomed {timeline_id, via} analytics (wheel debounced 400ms). Verified: typecheck + build + verify:globe + e2e 41/41 (added a zoom clamp/enable test; GS1 + canvas/palette unregressed). PRD §GS2 marked shipped. NOTE: local-107 (GS1) is still status:open here but GS1 is verifiably shipped (PRD §GS1 + the 'story plays on the globe' e2e) — flag for sync-time reconciliation.

data.title: Implement GLOBE-S GS1 — story-driven globe: beats rotate + zoom + skip the cursor (the headline)
data.description:
Wire the docked story reader's per-beat focus into the globe so playing a story flies the globe to where each beat happened and SKIPS the time cursor to when. The reader already renders over the globe (TimelineCanvas.tsx:1207) but its activeBeat/beatFocusId only drive the React-Flow StoryCamera (TimelineCanvas.tsx:1114) — the globe runs an independent clock and ignores the story. Refs: docs/product/prd/globe-stories.md §GS1.

### Scope
- New additive optional GlobeLens props: `storyFocus?: { id, lat, lng, instant } | null` (the current beat's focus node + its instant) and `storyMode?: boolean` (a reader is open over the globe).
- In TimelineCanvas, derive both from the EXISTING state: `focusNode` (the resolved beat-focus GraphNode, TimelineCanvas.tsx:500) when it carries lat/lng (fall back to the moment node, then null) → storyFocus; `reading` → storyMode. Pass into the GlobeLens render branch (TimelineCanvas.tsx:1150–1169).
- In GlobeLens, on a `storyFocus?.id` change (effect): set rotation target to [storyFocus.lng, storyFocus.lat] and zoom target to a story-zoom constant (~1.8×); ease both via the GS2 shared ease (runs with playback paused). SKIP the cursor: setCursorInstant(storyFocus.instant) + xRef.current = scale.toX(instant) → the scrubber thumb (bound to scale.toX(cursorInstant), GlobeLens.tsx:321–323) jumps to the beat. Markers appear/halo off cursorInstant already (GlobeLens.tsx:277–289), so the right things light up for free.
- On story end, ease back out to frame the story's focus set (fit-all).
- While storyMode: suppress the globe's own togglePlay autoplay (the reader's Play is the transport); the scrubber stays a progress readout; manual scrub still works (detaches, like userRotated).
- Reduced-motion: SNAP rotation/zoom/cursor to the beat target (no animated spin) — consistent with the reader's reduced-motion mode + the global reset.
- Off-map beat (OQ-S1, resolved: hold camera, still skip time — no fly-to-null).
- State that must survive a beat step / nodes prop change: cursorInstant/playing/userRotated/rAF stay local (GLOBE v1 §6 rule).

### Done when
With the globe open + a story playing, each beat eases rotation+zoom to the beat's focus coords and the scrubber thumb JUMPS to that beat's instant; story end eases back to frame the cast; an off-map beat holds the camera but still advances the cursor; reduced-motion snaps; no schema/MCP change; typecheck + build green; verify:globe + globe e2e unregressed.

data.title: Implement GLOBE-S GS3 — floating entity cards above markers (decluttered)
data.description:
Show 'what they are' on the globe: a compact card (type glyph + title, theme-accented) above markers, replacing the lone selected-marker `<text>` label (GlobeLens.tsx:368–372). The hard part is clutter — never label every marker at once. Refs: docs/product/prd/globe-stories.md §GS3.

### Scope
- Replace the single `selected && <text>` label with a `<GlobeLabels>` layer. Extend each entry in the `markers` memo (GlobeLens.tsx:268–294) with a `labelPriority`.
- Always-on labels: selected, active-span, and the current story-beat focus (GS1) — few + meaningful.
- Hover/keyboard-focus: any marker shows its full card (`hoveredId` local state; pointer-enter/leave on the marker `<g>`).
- Zoom-gated reveal: as GS2 zoom increases, show more cards via a greedy screen-space de-overlap (show a label only if no higher-priority shown label sits within N px). Priority: selected > active > story-focus > larger `size` > earlier.
- Back-hemisphere markers (already culled, GlobeLens.tsx:278) and not-yet-appeared markers (GlobeLens.tsx:277) get no card.
- Card render: prefer `<foreignObject>` (real DOM → CSS theming, the type glyph as an icon, ellipsis) with a plain SVG `<rect>`+`<text>` fallback for Safari quirks (Wren/Kael to pick). Type glyph reuses the canvas node icon mapping (person/org/place/work/event/period) so the language matches.

### Done when
Markers show floating type+title cards — always for selected/active/story-focus, on hover for any, zoom-gated for the rest with NO visible overlap on a dense (~50-node) globe; back-face + not-yet-appeared markers show none; typecheck + build green; verify:globe + globe e2e unregressed.

### Done 2026-06-13
Shipped (build + e2e verified; uncommitted). A foreignObject card layer (type glyph from the canvas/⌘K icon map + title, theme-accented, pointer-events:none) replaces the lone selected `<text>`. Declutter: always-on for selected/story-focus/active + the hovered marker; the rest revealed by a greedy screen-space de-overlap (LABEL_GAP_X/Y) sorted larger/earlier-first — zoom-gating falls out for free (markers reproject as the GS2 zoom grows). The PRIMARY card keeps the globe-marker-label hook (singular for the GS1 tests). OQ-S3: de-overlap is the cap. e2e: a cards+axis test added; globe 11/11 green. PRD §GS3 marked shipped.

data.title: Implement GLOBE-S GS4 — era band above the globe scrubber
data.description:

Founder confirmed 2026-06-12: 'era is period' → the band is sourced from `type === 'period'` span nodes (resolves OQ-S4). Refs: docs/product/prd/globe-stories.md §GS4.

### Scope

Greedy row-assignment for overlaps, ≤2 rows (more → '+n').

- Color: tint segments with `--color-accent-era` (the era token decoupled from influence purple — see the canvas node design-language); labels truncate, full name on hover/title.

The exact-cursor globe-date readout stays. OQ-S4: era=period. Corner-chip skipped (the active-segment highlight conveys it). e2e: dated-axis + era-ribbon tests added; globe 11/11 green. data.title: Implement STORY-CTX SC1 — cross-lens story context previews (display)
data.description:
Show the contextual axis the active lens isn't showing while reading a story: Timeline view → a mini-globe (WHERE), Globe view → a time-strip (WHEN). Front-end only — NO schema/migration/MCP change. Refs: docs/product/prd/story-context-previews.md (Phase 1 / SC1).

### Multi-reference model
A beat references many nodes (`{focusNodeId} ∪ relatedNodeIds`), each with its own place + instant. The preview plots the WHOLE referenced set (via the existing `nodeById` prop), not one subject: a PIN per located node + a MARKER per referenced node, focus highlighted, rest muted. Cap a busy beat ~6 pins (focus + nearest) + "+k more".

### Placement — 40px peek row
A slim 40px context row at the foot of the beat stage (beats only, not cover/end). Resting: 24px globe glyph + primary place + `+N places` (Timeline) / multi-marker strip + the beat's period on the right (Globe). Hover/tap in Timeline view rises the full 140px globe popover (all located pins, focus highlighted) — zero layout cost, no reflow.

### Components + wire
- New: `StoryContextPreview` (peek row), `MiniGlobe` (140px static, array of {lat,lng,focus} pins, framed to centroid, ~150ms fade between beats), `MiniTimeStrip` (linear over cast span, marker per ref, period via formatInstant/formatInstantRange).
- Wire `lensView` (+ `isOwner`) from TimelineCanvas → StoryReader (the one new prop).
- Extract shared `coordsToRotation(lat,lng) => [-lng,-lat]` (GS1/local-107 reuses it).
- REQUIRED companion fix: GlobeLens under-insets while reading → `rightInset = reading ? panelW.detail + panelW.story + 32 : displayNode ? panelW.detail : 0` (TimelineCanvas.tsx:1201). Ship-blocking for Globe-view reading.

### Degradation (per node)
Located → pinned + counted. Placeless → GEO_SCOPE_LABELS caption (no pin). All-unlocated beat → focus scope label / "No place set" + owner-only "Ask Claude to add one". The strip always works (every node has an instant).

### Analytics
story_context_preview_shown { timeline_id, story_id, beat_index, preview_type, located_count, ref_count }; story_context_backfill_opened { timeline_id, node_id }. (_clicked is SC2.)

### Done when
Timeline reading: foot row shows primary + +N; peek renders all located pins framed to centroid; placeless→scope label, all-unset→"No place set" + nudge. Globe reading: marker per ref + the beat's period on the right. Cover/end: no preview. coordsToRotation extracted; GlobeLens inset fix in. No schema/migration/MCP change; typecheck + build green; verified on the seeded (coordinated) Stoicism timeline.

### Follow-on
SC2 (portal tap: tap preview → switch lens pre-focused on the beat, snap-to-target via GlobeLens focusRotation; NOT GS1-gated) is the staged fast-follow, depends on this.

data.title: Add an auto-play toggle to the story reader
data.description:
Give the docked story reader a toggle to turn timed auto-advance on/off. Default ON preserves the Reels/Stories slideshow; off makes the reader fully manual (step with taps/arrows), identical to reduced-motion. Mirrors the existing read-aloud (`speak`) toggle. Pure front-end — no app/MCP/schema/migration.

### What landed (uncommitted)
- `StoryReader.tsx` — `Timer`/`TimerOff` header button (`data-testid="autoplay-toggle"`, aria 'Turn auto-play off/on'), before the read-aloud button; new `autoPlay`/`onAutoPlayChange` props.
- `useTimelineScale.ts` — `ScalePref.autoPlay` (default ON) added to the per-timeline pref (load + save).
- `TimelineCanvas.tsx` — `autoPlayStories` state lifted, reset on timeline switch, persisted, threaded into StoryReader + CanvasSettings.
- `CanvasSettings.tsx` — 'Auto-play stories' Switch row (`data-testid="autoplay-stories-toggle"`) above 'Read stories aloud'.

### Mechanic
One derived gate: `autoAdvance = autoPlay && !reduced`; `speechDrivesAdvance = autoAdvance && speak && supported`; `timerDrivesAdvance = autoAdvance && !speechDrivesAdvance`. The active progress segment animates (`is-active`) only when `timerDrivesAdvance`, else renders static (`is-current`). When auto-play is off but narration is on, each beat is still read aloud but does NOT step — `narrationAdvance` guards `goNext` on `autoPlay`. One advance source at a time.

### Verified
